A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same EPIC research work. Their text, equations, figures and results support comparison, including v2's Appendices A–E; v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original accuracy, latency, throughput, long-context and chunk-splitting experiments in Section 6.

after.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of LegoLink and LegoLink-0, serving performance, and CacheBlend runtime profiling in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming AttnLink to LegoLink, the stated selection rule changes from k/2 tokens on either side of each boundary to k initial tokens of each non-first chunk. V2 also introduces LegoLink-0: prepend four BOS tokens before cache generation, then remove them from non-first chunks before linking without recomputation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, HotpotQA, SAMSum, MultiNews and synthetic Needle-in-a-Haystack. The represented QA, summarization, few-shot and retrieval tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding accuracy–latency comparisons retain FR, Naive and CacheBlend at recomputation ratios 1%, 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% (v1 Figure 6; v2 Figure 4). LegoLink-0 is an added proposed-method variant, not a new external baseline.

E3.justification: V1 specifies H800-80GB hardware, with an A100-40GB exception for asynchronous experiments; v2 specifies A100-80GB. V2 changes synchronous SAMSum and Needle chunking to 512 tokens and revises recomputation budgets. Its long-context protocol is internally inconsistent: Figure 7 says 512-token chunks, while Section 4.6 says 1024. These are reported setting changes, not proof that every experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 removes the semantic-versus-512-token splitting analysis on SAMSum and HotpotQA from v1 Section 6.6/Figure 9. It adds the dummy-token intervention, attention-map and output-failure analyses for LegoLink-0 in Section 4.4, plus layer-level CacheBlend runtime profiling in Appendix A.

E5.justification: Both asynchronous evaluations report averages and standard deviations from five experiments (v1 Figure 7; v2 Figure 6). V2 adds no seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance testing; the new runtime averages do not establish a changed uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the main accuracy–latency results under revised settings, adds LegoLink-0 results, and changes the reported sufficient budget from AttnLink-20 to LegoLink-2. Splitting results disappear and runtime breakdowns are added. Figure 8's overhead annotations span 16.37%–63.56%, although Appendix A states a 17.68% minimum. The headline 8× TTFT and 7× throughput claims remain.

T1.justification: V2 Section 2.3 explicitly distinguishes CacheBlend's O(N²) time complexity from O(N) memory complexity, whereas v1 groups time and resource complexity under O(N²). The selective-attention equations and main recomputation-complexity argument remain essentially unchanged; no formal proofs are added.

C1.justification: V1 presents AttnLink and customizable KVSplit as two key innovations. V2 removes KVSplit from the central contribution claims and centers the paper on LegoLink, including the possibility of zero-overhead linking. The headline latency, throughput and accuracy-loss claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 argues that query and decoded tokens can aggregate information across chunks, reducing the importance of missing cross-chunk attention during cache generation. It newly discusses prolonged irrelevant outputs as an accuracy and efficiency failure. Chunking shifts from a demonstrated central design benefit to an incompletely explored future direction.

D1.justification: Most vLLM, storage and cache-API implementation details survive in Appendices B–C. V2 replaces the description of two implemented KVSplit options with a statement that this phase is omitted, and adds the attention-map layer/head identification and the vLLM block-size rationale for k=16. Hardware and software specifications are also revised.

R1.justification: Most related work is retained. V2 shifts its critique of CacheBlend from rigid chunking toward runtime token-selection overhead and removes the Vaswani and Pope background references. The additional StreamingLLM reference entry corresponds to the already-cited attention-sink work.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction, background and algorithm narrative, foregrounding algorithm analysis. System design, implementation and dataset-distribution material move into appendices, and the evaluation loses its explicit RQ structure. Terminology changes throughout from AttnLink to LegoLink.

P2.justification: V2 reorganizes the accuracy–latency grid, revises legends and axes, updates the algorithm illustration, and adds zero-overhead attention and runtime-breakdown figures. V1's caching-category table and splitting figure disappear. Architecture and distribution figures move to appendices, alongside a substantial document-template change.

improvement.justification: V2's dummy-token intervention provides a more direct test of the attention-sink explanation, while its output-failure discussion better qualifies applicability. These strengthen support for the central mechanism. The gain is limited by removal of the chunking analysis and new reporting inconsistencies: 512 versus 1024 tokens in the long-context experiment, and Appendix A's minimum overhead conflicting with Figure 8.
